structure.description: Top-level directory for global stylesheets and design tokens. Houses CSS files that are imported once at the application entry point (e.g. tokens.css) and apply app-wide rather than per-component. Component-scoped styles live in CSS Modules alongside their components.

Global CSS file that defines the extended design-token system used across the application. Adds to the tokens already declared in src/index.css with shared design system values and calculator-specific sizing. Defines on :root: a spacing scale (--space-2xs through --space-2xl, 4px-48px), a border-radius scale (--radius-sm/md/lg/full), a shadow scale (--shadow-sm/md/lg) using translucent black layered per the existing --shadow convention, semantic color tokens (--color-success, --color-error, --color-warning plus their -bg variants), transition durations (--transition-fast 150ms / --transition-base 200ms / --transition-slow 300ms), a z-index scale (--z-base/elevated/overlay), and calculator-specific sizing tokens (--calc-width 22rem, --calc-button-size 3.5rem, --calc-display-min-height 6rem, --calc-gap 0.625rem, --calc-button-radius). All values are defined as CSS custom properties on :root so that every CSS Module and the existing index.css can reference them via var(--token-name). Imported once in main.tsx immediately after the existing './index.css' import so tokens are available before any module styles evaluate.

Top-level directory for shared, reusable UI building blocks used across multiple features. Subdivided into 'common/' for primitive components (Button, Input, Modal, etc.) and 'layout/' for page-level layout wrappers (PageLayout, Header, Footer, etc.). Nothing feature-specific lives here.

Directory for primitive, reusable UI components designed to be composed anywhere in the app. Currently contains the Button primitive. These components are visually styled according to the design system and accept props for behavior; they own no application state.
Directory for the Button component, its colocated types, and its CSS Module. All Button-related files live here so the component is self-contained and easy to relocate.

Type definitions for the Button component. Exports the ButtonVariant string union ('number' | 'operation' | 'equals' | 'clear' | 'utility') used to drive visual styling, and the ButtonProps interface. ButtonProps fields: label (ReactNode — the visible button content, typically a string or symbol), onClick (() => void — required click handler), variant (ButtonVariant, optional, defaults to 'number'), span (1 | 2, optional, defaults to 1, used by the Keypad to make the '0' button span two grid columns), active (boolean, optional, defaults to false; when true applies a 'selected' visual treatment — used by the Keypad to highlight the currently pending operator), disabled (boolean, optional, defaults to false), ariaLabel (string, optional; falls back to a stringified label when omitted so screen readers always get a meaningful announcement). Consumed by Button.tsx for prop typing and by Keypad.types.ts (which re-uses the ButtonVariant type).

Renders a reusable, styled <button> element. Props (ButtonProps): label, onClick, variant (defaults to 'number'), span (defaults to 1, applied as grid-column: span N), active (defaults to false, applied as data-attribute for the active visual state), disabled, ariaLabel. Implementation: returns a single <button> with the className from Button.module.css, data-variant, data-active, and disabled attributes set; aria-label defaults to String(label) when ariaLabel is not provided. The native <button> element supplies built-in keyboard activation (Space/Enter), focus management, and disabled handling so no custom event logic is required. All visual styling — base layout, variant colors, hover/active/focus states, press feedback, and the span modifier — lives in the colocated Button.module.css. This component is consumed by the calculator Keypad and is designed to be used by any future feature that needs a styled button.

CSS Module styles for the Button component. Defines: a .button base rule applying display: flex, align-items/justify-content: center, min-height: var(--calc-button-size) (ensures a comfortable touch target), border-radius: var(--calc-button-radius), border: none, cursor: pointer, user-select: none, font: inherit, color: inherit, and a transition on transform/background-color/box-shadow using var(--transition-fast). Variant styles via [data-variant="..."] attribute selectors reference design tokens: 'number' uses a neutral surface (var(--bg) over a slightly elevated background), 'operation' uses the accent (var(--accent) text on var(--accent-bg) with var(--accent-border) on hover), 'equals' uses the primary accent (var(--accent) background with white text and a subtle var(--shadow-md) elevation), 'clear' uses a warm/attention color (var(--color-error) text on a muted background), and 'utility' uses a subtle background. Active modifier ([data-active="true"]) applies a pressed/inset look. :active applies transform: scale(0.97) for press feedback. :focus-visible applies a 2px solid var(--accent) outline with 2px offset for keyboard users. [data-span="2"] applies grid-column: span 2. :disabled applies opacity 0.5 and cursor: not-allowed. All values reference tokens from src/styles/tokens.css and src/index.css — no hardcoded color or spacing literals.

Barrel file for the Button directory. Re-exports the named Button component from './Button' and the ButtonProps + ButtonVariant types from './Button.types'. Allows consumers to write `import { Button } from './components/common/Button'` or `import { Button } from './components/common'` without reaching into the internal files.

Barrel file for the src/components/common/ directory. Re-exports everything from the Button subdirectory (Button, ButtonProps, ButtonVariant) to provide a single import surface for shared UI primitives.

Directory for page-level layout components that provide consistent chrome (centering, padding, background, titles) wrapping feature content. Currently contains the PageLayout wrapper. New layout components (Header, Footer, Sidebar, etc.) belong here.
Directory for the PageLayout component and its colocated files. PageLayout is the single shell that wraps the application's main content.

Page-level layout wrapper that provides consistent centering, background, padding, and an optional title/subtitle for the entire page. Props: children (ReactNode — required, the page content), title (string, optional, defaults to 'Calculator'), subtitle (string, optional, omitted when not provided). Renders a
element with className from PageLayout.module.css containing a header (
) with the title as an

and the optional subtitle as a muted

, followed by the children. The wrapper uses the --heading font for the title (inheriting the existing h1 styles from index.css) and respects semantic landmarks (

,
). The component is purely presentational and owns no state. Consumed by App.tsx as the top-level wrapper around the Calculator feature.

CSS Module styles for the PageLayout component. Defines: the .layout main element as a flex column with min-height: 100svh, padding from --space-md (--space-sm on small screens), background using the global --bg token, and a centered inner content area (max-width chosen so the calculator card fits comfortably). The .header block has a bottom margin of --space-xl, the h1 inherits from index.css but is given a small additional letter-spacing and color reset to ensure consistent rendering, and the .subtitle uses --text color with --space-xs top margin. On viewports under 480px the outer padding reduces and the title shrinks via a clamp() in the inherited h1 styles. All spacing/colors reference design tokens from src/styles/tokens.css and src/index.css.
Barrel file for the PageLayout directory. Re-exports the named PageLayout component so it can be imported as 'from "./components/layout/PageLayout"' or 'from "./components/layout"'.
Barrel file for the src/components/layout/ directory. Re-exports PageLayout from its subdirectory so consumers can import it via 'from "./components/layout"'.

Top-level directory for feature modules. Each feature is self-contained with its own components, hooks, utils, and types directory. Features are independent vertical slices — the calculator is one such slice; future features (settings, history, etc.) would each get their own sibling folder.

The calculator feature module. Contains everything calculator-specific: types, utility functions, custom hooks, presentational components (Display, Keypad), the orchestrating Calculator component, and the feature barrel. The feature exposes a single top-level component (Calculator) via its index.ts barrel.

Directory for type definitions specific to the calculator feature. Houses calculator.types.ts which centralizes every type used across the feature so the reducer, hooks, and components all share a single source of truth.

Centralized type definitions for the calculator feature. Exports: Operator — string union 'add' | 'subtract' | 'multiply' | 'divide' (used in state, action payloads, and operator config); ErrorCode — string union 'DIVIDE_BY_ZERO' | 'INVALID_INPUT' (used by CalculatorError); CalculatorAction — discriminated union covering all possible user actions: { type: 'DIGIT'; payload: string }, { type: 'DECIMAL' }, { type: 'OPERATOR'; payload: Operator }, { type: 'EQUALS' }, { type: 'CLEAR' }, { type: 'DELETE' }, { type: 'TOGGLE_SIGN' }, { type: 'PERCENT' }; CalculatorState — interface with fields display (string — current value shown in the main display), expression (string — pending operation text shown above the value, e.g. '12 +'), previousValue (number | null — the stored operand), operator (Operator | null — the pending operator), waitingForNewValue (boolean — true after an operator is pressed, signals the next digit should replace the display), justEvaluated (boolean — true immediately after '=' so the next digit resets the calculator), error (string | null — null when healthy, a user-facing error message otherwise). Consumed by useCalculator (state and action types), the reducer, Display, Keypad, useKeyboardInput, and operatorConfig.

Directory for pure utility functions used by the calculator feature. Contains calculate (binary arithmetic), formatNumber (display formatting), and operatorConfig (operator metadata). All files in this directory are side-effect-free and easily unit-testable.

Pure utility that performs binary arithmetic for the calculator. Exports: CalculatorError — class extending Error with an additional optional code: ErrorCode field; calculate(a: number, b: number, operator: Operator): number — returns a + b for 'add', a - b for 'subtract', a * b for 'multiply', and a / b for 'divide'. When operator is 'divide' and b is exactly 0, throws a CalculatorError with code 'DIVIDE_BY_ZERO'. Has no side effects, no React, and no I/O — trivially unit-testable. Consumed exclusively by the calculatorReducer inside useCalculator.

Pure utility for formatting numbers for display in the calculator. Exports: MAX_DISPLAY_LENGTH — number constant 12 (the maximum number of characters shown on the display before falling back to exponential notation); formatNumber(value: number, maxLength?: number — defaults to MAX_DISPLAY_LENGTH): string. Behavior: if !isFinite(value) returns the literal 'Error'; if the absolute value is >= 1e12 or (non-zero and < 1e-6), returns value.toExponential(5); otherwise rounds via parseFloat(value.toPrecision(12)) to strip floating-point artifacts (e.g. 0.1 + 0.2 → '0.3'), stringifies, and if the result still exceeds maxLength falls back to value.toPrecision(maxLength - 2). Pure function with no side effects. Consumed by calculatorReducer when finalizing a result for display.

Centralized configuration for calculator operators. Exports: OperatorConfig — interface with fields type (Operator), symbol (string — the typographic character to display, e.g. '+' or '−'), label (string — short label, e.g. 'Add'), ariaLabel (string — accessible label for screen readers); OPERATORS — Record<Operator, OperatorConfig> mapping each operator to its display metadata. Uses typographic Unicode symbols (U+002B '+', U+2212 '−' for minus, U+00D7 '×' for multiply, U+00F7 '÷' for divide) for better visual presentation than ASCII '-', '*', '/'. Consumed by Keypad.tsx to render operator buttons with consistent symbols and ARIA labels, and by Display.tsx when composing the expression preview.

Directory for custom React hooks specific to the calculator feature. Houses useCalculator (state management) and useKeyboardInput (global keyboard listener). Hooks are colocated with the feature that owns them rather than living in a global hooks/ directory.

Custom React hook that owns all calculator state and exposes a dispatch function for triggering actions. Internally uses useReducer with a module-level calculatorReducer (defined in this same file) and a constant initialState: CalculatorState = { display: '0', expression: '', previousValue: null, operator: null, waitingForNewValue: false, justEvaluated: false, error: null }. The reducer handles every CalculatorAction case: DIGIT — appends a digit to display, but if waitingForNewValue or justEvaluated is true it replaces the display, and if the resulting display would exceed MAX_DISPLAY_LENGTH the action is ignored; DECIMAL — adds a '.' only if the current display does not already contain one; OPERATOR — if there is already a pending previousValue + operator, calculates the pending operation first (chained operations), then stores the new previousValue, sets operator, sets expression, and sets waitingForNewValue; EQUALS — calculates the pending operation if previousValue and operator are both set, formats the result via formatNumber, sets justEvaluated, and clears the pending operator; CLEAR — returns initialState verbatim; DELETE — strips the last character of display, falling back to '0' if the display has only one character or is already '0'; TOGGLE_SIGN — negates the current display value if it is not '0'; PERCENT — divides the current display value by 100. All calculate() errors are caught and stored in state.error; if the user enters a second operator after an error, the CLEAR effect runs. The hook's exported signature is function useCalculator(): { state: CalculatorState; dispatch: React.Dispatch<CalculatorAction> } — the consumer (Calculator.tsx) wraps dispatch in useCallback for stability.

Custom React hook that attaches a global keydown event listener to the window and translates keyboard keys into CalculatorAction dispatches. Signature: function useKeyboardInput(onAction: (action: CalculatorAction) => void, enabled?: boolean — defaults to true): void. Key mappings (case-insensitive for letters): '0'-'9' → DIGIT with the digit as payload; numpad '0'-'9' → same; '+' and numpad '+' → OPERATOR 'add'; '-' and numpad '-' → OPERATOR 'subtract'; '*' and numpad '*' → OPERATOR 'multiply'; '/' and numpad '/' → OPERATOR 'divide'; 'Enter', '=' and numpad 'Enter' → EQUALS; 'Escape', 'c', 'C' → CLEAR; 'Backspace' → DELETE; '.' and numpad '.' → DECIMAL; '%' → PERCENT. The listener early-returns and does nothing when any of e.ctrlKey, e.metaKey, or e.altKey is true (so browser shortcuts like Ctrl+R still work), and calls e.preventDefault() on the matched keys that would otherwise have a default browser action (e.g. '/' to prevent Firefox quick-find). The listener is attached only when enabled is true; the effect cleans up the listener on unmount and when its dependencies change. The consumer is expected to pass a stable onAction (memoized via useCallback) so the effect does not re-run on every render.

Directory for calculator-specific React components. Currently contains the Display (the read-out area) and Keypad (the button grid) — both are presentational and receive all behavior via props. New calculator-specific components (e.g. HistoryPanel, MemoryIndicator) would live here as siblings.
Directory for the Display component and its colocated files. Display is the read-out area at the top of the calculator showing the current value and pending expression.

Type definitions for the Display component. Exports DisplayProps interface: value (string — required, the main numeric value to show prominently), expression (string — required, the pending expression text to show smaller above the value; pass an empty string to hide the line entirely), hasError (boolean — optional, defaults to false; when true applies error styling and a brief shake animation, and the value is treated as the error message). Consumed by Display.tsx for prop typing.

Renders the calculator's read-out area. Props (DisplayProps): value, expression, hasError (defaults to false). Renders an <output> element (semantic for calculated output) with className from Display.module.css, role='status' and aria-live='polite' so screen readers announce value changes, and an aria-label='Calculator display'. Inside: a small <div> with the expression text (hidden via conditional render when expression is an empty string) styled as a muted secondary line, and a large <div> with the value text styled as the main number. Both texts are right-aligned, use the --mono font token, and the value line uses overflow: hidden + text-overflow: ellipsis + white-space: nowrap to prevent layout breakage. When hasError is true, the wrapper receives an 'error' modifier that switches the color to var(--color-error) and triggers a 0.4s shake keyframe animation defined in Display.module.css. The component is purely presentational — owns no state and emits no events. Consumed by Calculator.tsx, which passes state.error (when present) or state.display as value, state.expression as expression, and !!state.error as hasError.

CSS Module styles for the Display component. Defines: a .display container with flex column layout, right-aligned text, padding from --space-md, background using a token-defined display surface (var(--calc-display-bg) or a derived value), border-radius from --radius-md on the top corners, and min-height: var(--calc-display-min-height) to prevent layout shift when the value changes length. The .expression line uses a small font size (clamp(0.875rem, 2vw, 1rem)), muted color from --text, font-weight 400, line-height tight, overflow hidden with text-overflow ellipsis, and a min-height so the line does not collapse when empty. The .value line uses a large responsive font size (clamp(1.75rem, 8vw, 3rem)), font-weight 500, --mono font, right-aligned, text-overflow ellipsis, white-space nowrap, and a smooth color transition. The .display[data-error='true'] modifier applies color: var(--color-error) and triggers a brief shake keyframe (translateX +/- 4px) over 0.4s. All values reference design tokens from src/styles/tokens.css.
Barrel file for the Display directory. Re-exports the named Display component and DisplayProps type so consumers can import via the directory path.
Directory for the Keypad component and its colocated files. Keypad renders the 4x5 grid of calculator buttons.

Type definitions for the Keypad component. Exports: KeypadButtonConfig — interface describing a single keypad cell: label (string — the visible text), action (CalculatorAction — dispatched when the button is pressed), variant (ButtonVariant — drives the button's color), span (1 | 2, optional, defaults to 1 — used to make the '0' button span two columns), ariaLabel (string, optional — falls back to label for screen readers). KeypadProps — interface: onAction ((action: CalculatorAction) => void — required, called with the action from the pressed button), activeOperator (Operator | null, optional — the currently pending operator; when set, the matching operator button receives the 'active' visual state to indicate it is the pending operation). Consumed by Keypad.tsx for prop typing and to type the module-level KEYPAD_LAYOUT constant.

Renders the calculator's 4-column by 5-row button grid. Props (KeypadProps): onAction, activeOperator (optional, defaults to null). The keypad layout is defined as a module-level KEYPAD_LAYOUT: KeypadButtonConfig[][] constant in the same file (Row 1: AC, ±, %, ÷; Row 2: 7, 8, 9, ×; Row 3: 4, 5, 6, −; Row 4: 1, 2, 3, +; Row 5: 0 (span 2), ., =). The OPERATORS config from utils/operatorConfig is used to populate operator button symbols and ariaLabels. The component renders a <div> with the className from Keypad.module.css acting as a CSS grid container; each cell is rendered by mapping over the layout and returning a <Button> from the shared common/Button component with the configured label, variant, span, ariaLabel, and active flag (active is true when the button's action.type === 'OPERATOR' && action.payload === activeOperator). Clicking any button invokes onAction(button.action). The component is purely presentational and owns no state. Consumed by Calculator.tsx, which passes a stable dispatch wrapper as onAction and state.operator as activeOperator.

CSS Module styles for the Keypad component. Defines a .keypad container as a 4-column CSS grid with grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr) and gap: var(--calc-gap). The grid has padding from --space-sm so the buttons do not touch the card edge. On very narrow viewports (under 360px) the gap shrinks via a media query. The component does not style the individual buttons themselves — visual treatment is delegated to the shared Button component and its CSS Module. Bottom corners of the keypad have a small radius matching the calculator card so the bottom row of buttons visually nests into the card's rounded bottom.
Barrel file for the Keypad directory. Re-exports the named Keypad component and the KeypadProps and KeypadButtonConfig types so consumers can import via the directory path.

Top-level orchestrating component for the calculator feature. Composes Display and Keypad, wires them to the calculator state, and integrates keyboard input. Implementation: calls useCalculator() to get { state, dispatch }; wraps dispatch in a useCallback as a stable onAction (the callback depends only on the stable dispatch, so the keyboard listener attaches once); calls useKeyboardInput(onAction) so global key presses drive the same dispatch; renders a single <section> with className from Calculator.module.css, aria-label='Calculator', containing a <Display> (passing state.error ?? state.display as value, state.expression as expression, and !!state.error as hasError) and a <Keypad> (passing onAction and state.operator as activeOperator). Owns no state of its own — all state is encapsulated in the useCalculator hook. This is the single component App.tsx renders inside the PageLayout.

CSS Module styles for the Calculator component. Defines the .calculator card container: width: 100% with max-width: var(--calc-width) (22rem on desktop), background slightly elevated from --bg (using a token-defined surface or subtle gradient), border-radius: var(--radius-lg), padding: var(--space-md), box-shadow: var(--shadow-lg) for elevation against the page background, overflow: hidden to clip child corners, and a subtle border using --border for definition in light mode (borderless but shadowed in dark mode via a prefers-color-scheme media query referencing the existing tokens). Internal layout: flex column with gap: var(--space-sm) so the Display sits above the Keypad with consistent spacing. On viewports under 480px the card takes nearly full available width with reduced padding and a smaller shadow. All values reference design tokens from src/styles/tokens.css.

Barrel file for the calculator feature. Re-exports the named Calculator component (the top-level feature component) so App.tsx can import it as 'from "./features/calculator"' without reaching into the internal file path.

modifiedFiles.description: Application entry point. The only change is the addition of a single side-effect import of the new design-tokens stylesheet immediately after the existing './index.css' import, so the extended token set (--space-*, --radius-*, --shadow-*, --color-*, --calc-*, --transition-*, --z-*) is globally available before any module CSS evaluates. No other logic, imports, or JSX are changed; createRoot/StrictMode/App rendering are untouched.
modifiedFiles.reason: The new design-tokens stylesheet must be loaded globally alongside the existing index.css so component CSS Modules can reference the new tokens.

modifiedFiles.description: Root application component. Replaced in full: removed the Vite-template imports (useState, the reactLogo/viteLogo/heroImg asset imports, and the './App.css' import), and added imports for PageLayout (from './components/layout') and Calculator (from './features/calculator'). The function body now returns a single <PageLayout> wrapping the <Calculator> feature — no useState, no inline assets, no starter counter logic. The default export is preserved unchanged so the existing import in main.tsx ('import App from './App.tsx'') continues to work without modification to main.tsx.
modifiedFiles.reason: App.tsx is being repurposed from a Vite starter demo to the real application shell that renders the calculator feature inside the shared page layout.

modifiedFiles.description: The previous contents of this file described CSS for the Vite starter template (selectors like .hero, .framework, .vite, .ticks, #center, .counter) — every one of those selectors referenced DOM that no longer exists in the new App.tsx. The file has been cleared and replaced with a single comment noting that it is intentionally empty because the new App.tsx no longer imports it. Keeping an empty file in place (rather than deleting it) avoids changing the file tree while ensuring the misleading dead styles cannot accidentally be re-introduced. No JS or TypeScript file imports this stylesheet anymore.
modifiedFiles.reason: The original App.css content described selectors for DOM that has been removed; leaving it in place would be misleading dead code, and the file is no longer imported from App.tsx.

notes: No path aliases are configured in tsconfig.app.json (no 'paths' or 'baseUrl' entries, only 'include': ['src']), so every new file uses relative imports resolved from its own directory. The deepest relative path is four levels up (used by the Keypad to reach src/components/common/Button).

CSS Modules are used for all new component styles (per Vite/React convention and because no other styling approach is configured). Global styles come from the existing src/index.css plus the new src/styles/tokens.css; no Tailwind, styled-components, or other libraries are introduced.

The existing src/index.css is intentionally left untouched — it already provides a useful token foundation (--text, --text-h, --bg, --border, --accent, --sans, --heading, --mono, plus #root/body/h1/h2/p global styles) that the new components reference via CSS Modules. Only its unused .counter, .hero, .ticks, #center selectors remain as harmless dead CSS; cleaning them is out of scope.

App.tsx is the only component kept as a default export to match the existing import in main.tsx. All other components in the new structure use named exports for clearer imports, easier barrel-file re-exports, and better tree-shaking.

The tsconfig has 'verbatimModuleSyntax': true and 'erasableSyntaxOnly': true, so type-only imports must use `import type { ... }` and the codebase avoids enums, namespaces, and parameter properties. The calculator types module (calculator.types.ts) uses string-union types exclusively, and the operator config uses a const Record rather than an enum.
react-router-dom is already installed in package.json but is not used by the calculator feature; it is left available for future routing needs.
